$comment: C5. Checked after everything else and wins unconditionally. A URL containing any of these is passed through entirely untouched — no substitution, and no stripping either. See PRODUCT.md §9.5 and §11.1.
$policy: Ambiguity resolves toward inclusion. Substitution causes a site to act on a wrong value, where stripping usually causes it to fall back to a default, so this list is deliberately broader than the equivalent list in a subtractive tool.

auth.$why: A fabricated credential or flow parameter attacks the user's own session.

oauth.$why: OAuth and OIDC parameters are load-bearing for the whole handshake.

signature.$why: Signed URLs fail closed. Changing any component produces a 403, not a log entry.

function.$why: Ordinary query fields. Substituting these changes what the user asked for.

commerce.$why: PRODUCT.md §11.1 constraint 1. Substituting one affiliate's identifier for another's redirects a commission to a party that did not earn it. This is fraud, not privacy, and it is the hardest line in the product.

payment.$why: Anything that can be part of a transaction record.

$matching: Names are compared case-insensitively after trimming. A URL carrying any listed name is exempt in full — the extension does not attempt to rewrite the other parameters around it, because a URL containing a signature or an OAuth handshake is one whose exact shape is likely to matter.
